title: WHAT HAPPENS IF… · #01

lines.text: This is what happens if you swallow your gum.
Benny just did it. Gulp. Let's follow it inside.
Down the throat it goes. A few seconds, and splash.
It lands in his stomach. Acid everywhere.
The sugar and flavor? Absorbed. Gone.
But the gum base is basically rubber. Your body can't digest it.
So does it stay inside for seven years? Nope. Total myth.
Your gut just pushes it along, like everything else you eat.
Small intestine. Then the large one. Slowly, slowly.
In about one to three days, it leaves the usual way.
The only real danger? Swallowing lots of gum, every single day.
Doctors have found gum blockages in kids who did exactly that.
So one piece is fine. But now that you know where it goes... would you swallow it?

sources: Duke Health: stomach empties in 30–120 min; 7-year claim false
Cleveland Clinic: gum base is indigestible and passes through; not 7 years
Inverse/HowStuffWorks: ~1–3 days; rare blockage cases in children who swallowed several pieces daily
KidsHealth: occasional swallowed gum is harmless
